description:
PearGuard is a privacy-focused, peer-to-peer parental control app. The parent device pairs directly with the child device — no accounts, no servers, no subscriptions. Your family's activity data lives only on the devices you pair.

PearGuard is designed for families where the child uses an Android device. The parent can use Android or iOS.

FEATURES

Screen Time Limits
Set daily time budgets and bedtime windows on the child device.

Per-App Policies
Allow, block, or time-limit individual apps by category or one at a time.

Activity View
See what's been used and when, directly from the parent device.

Time Requests
The child can request extra time; the parent approves or denies from their device.

Privacy First
No account creation. No email address. No tracking. No ads. Activity never leaves the paired devices.

Open Source
PearGuard is free and open source. Source code is available on GitHub.

PERMISSIONS

Camera — used to scan QR invite codes when pairing with a child device.
Photo Library — used to set profile photos.
whatsNew:
## What's Changed

  ### Improvements

  - quick setup by age: pick Young child, Pre-teen, Teen or Allowlist only and get a sensible starting set of limits, categories and a bedtime instead of building it by hand
  - time windows per app: say "games only 4pm to 6pm" or "social blocked during school hours" for a single app, on the days you choose
  - free time: pause every rule for an hour, a few hours or the rest of the day for a sick day, a trip or a reward, then protection turns itself back on
  - give bonus screen time whenever you like, straight from the dashboard or the child's page, without waiting for your child to ask
  - blocking on Android is faster and easier on the battery

  ### Bug Fixes

  - overnight bedtimes set for certain days now cover the whole night, instead of blocking the morning and leaving the small hours free
  - your child's daily screen time now counts every app they use, not only the ones already listed in your rules
  - winding a computer's clock or timezone back no longer hands back screen time that was already used, and you get told when it happens
  - changing the clock just after switching Wi-Fi on or off is now spotted as tampering
  - a child's computer that restarts while you are offline now keeps enforcing your rules straight away, instead of allowing everything until you next connect
  - you are now told when protection fails to start, gets stuck or stops watching on your child's computer, rather than the dashboard quietly showing everything as fine
  - you are also told when the protection service on an Android device is switched on but not actually running
  - a newly installed app is now held for your approval instead of being freely usable until you next connect
  - apps whose name happens to contain "sms", "dialer" or "messaging", such as Signal, are no longer exempt from every rule
  - a blocked child can no longer get back in by opening an invite meant for someone else
  - extra time you approve now reaches your child even if their device was offline at the time
  - pairing no longer sits on "Connecting to child..." forever, and an invite link opened twice no longer counts twice
  - a second parent is no longer removed by mistake when two parents share a name
  - apps your child uninstalls now disappear from your rules instead of lingering
  - the block screen now updates when your rules change, so a locked device can no longer offer a way out of the lock
  - activity is filed under the day it actually happened, even across midnight or a timezone difference
  - names and messages with accents or emoji are no longer scrambled or silently dropped
  - Linux apps no longer show up twice in your rules
  - fixed a blank or frozen screen when opening the app, or returning to it after a while
  - alerts and updates are no longer lost if the screen reloads behind the scenes
  - the app no longer hangs waiting for a reply that never comes, and recovers on its own
  - storage on a paired computer no longer grows without limit, and old bonus-time records are tidied away

  ### Other

  - Windows and Linux builds are now produced in one place, so both stay in step
